description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a large language model’s response to external feedback, as presented in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.86 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The “Final Accuracy” (blue solid line with circle markers) remains consistently high, hovering just below 1.0 across all initial confidence levels, with slight fluctuations and error bars indicating small variance. The “Initial Accuracy” (green dashed line with square markers) starts at approximately 0.65 at initial confidence 0.86, rises gradually to a peak near 0.92 at confidence 0.97, then declines to about 0.77 at confidence 1.00, showing a non-monotonic trend with visible error bars. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange dash-dotted line with diamond markers) begins at ~0.3 at confidence 0.86, decreases to a minimum near 0.05 around confidence 0.93–0.95, then rises again to ~0.2 at confidence 1.00, indicating that the model’s improvement from feedback is smallest at moderate-to-high initial confidence levels and recovers slightly at the highest confidence. All lines include vertical error bars, suggesting variability in measurements across trials or prompts.
